overview: Elam was one of the oldest civilizations in the world, centered in southwestern Iran around the city of Susa. It developed a unique language unrelated to any known family, built monumental ziggurats and maintained a complex rivalry with Mesopotamia for three millennia.

items.text: The ziggurat at Chogha Zanbil constructed, one of the best-preserved stepped pyramids in the world.
Sophisticated irrigation systems supported agriculture in the Khuzestan plains.
Elamite bronze work, cylinder seals and carved stone reliefs show distinctive artistic traditions.
Proto-Elamite script, one of the earliest writing systems, remains undeciphered.
A pantheon headed by the goddess Kiririsha and the god Inshushinak, patron of Susa.
Royal succession followed matrilineal patterns unusual in the ancient Near East.
Chogha Zanbil is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
Elamite administrative practices influenced the later Achaemenid Empire.

fall.text: Elam was absorbed into the rising Achaemenid Persian Empire, with Susa becoming one of its capitals.
